findings.issue: parseHandle casts the parsed `ref` wholesale (`ref as ResourceRef`) with NO shape validation — it copies whatever object sits under the `ref` key. A crafted/tampered wire string `{tenantId,handleId,ref:{kind:'record',...,data:{ssn:'secret'}}}` deserializes into a validly-BRANDED ObjectHandle whose `ref` carries a record payload, and serializeHandle re-emits it intact. Because assertVariableValue short-circuits to ok:true on isObjectHandle(value) BEFORE any structural inspection, that forged-but-branded handle smuggles the payload past the variable-write guard. This is a latent opacity-bypass for any UNTRUSTED wire input. It is a nit, not blocking, because: (a) no exported AC/FF claims parseHandle validates tampered input — AC-7 only asserts the honest serialize->parse round-trip of well-formed handles, which holds; (b) parseHandle has zero consumers in this static-now module (no untrusted-input path exists yet); (c) all in-scope invariants hold. But the wire form is exactly the cross-trust-boundary representation the opacity invariant must eventually survive, and T-0021/T-0027 (which consume the wire form) would inherit this gap silently.
findings.suggestion: Harden parseHandle to reconstruct `ref` from validated identity components only (switch on kind, copy exactly the known UUID fields, reject unknown keys / a `data`/`fields`/`payload`/`view` sibling), OR have makeHandle/parseHandle strip `ref` to its known identity fields, AND/OR have assertVariableValue inspect handle.ref structurally even for branded handles. Add an adversarial round-trip test asserting an injected ref.data is stripped or rejected. Tracked as a spawned follow-up so T-0021 does not inherit it.
